hops.note: UBI-231. Scoped narrower than write-artifacts' full three-check coverage: this hop tracks missing_field_description only. Real, live-recomputed missing_field_description before batch 1: 613. Unlike gcp, aws has no common_aws_fields.py dictionary tier -- every field here is individually authored, checked against real AWS CloudFormation resource reference documentation for anything uncommon rather than guessed. aws is a long tail: 208 resources across roughly 90 real services, most services carrying only one or two gapped resources -- batched by service, largest first, expect this to run slower per field than gcp's clusters did.

doc_tree_quirks.issue: its own 10 gapped fields are NOT part of the quicksight service and were never touched by batch 3. Its real published page lives under resource-reference/aws/quick/ (service directory "quick"), a sibling of, not a child of, resource-reference/aws/data/quicksight/ where the rest of the quicksight resources live. A resuming session filtering the missing_field_description list by a naive quicksight/quick_sight substring match will see this resource's fields as still open and correctly conclude they are -- but must resolve its real page under the quick/ directory, not quicksight/, when writing text for it. Not a miss in batch 3; a separate, pre-existing doc-tree naming inconsistency, still unresolved as of batch 4.

doc_tree_quirks.scope: general -- discovered while scoping the long-tail batches after batch 4. Filed as UBI-232 (https://linear.app/ubiquex/issue/UBI-232) since this is a published-corpus bug affecting readers, not just a batching hazard -- UBI-232 is the real fix, this note is a workaround record only.
doc_tree_quirks.issue: quick/quicksight is one instance of a broader, pre-existing doc-tree naming inconsistency: the resource-reference/aws page generator splits some multi-word AWS service names across two directories instead of one, using the first token as its own top-level directory. Confirmed instances beyond quick/quicksight: resource-reference/aws/cloud/ holds three CloudFront resources (front-connection-function, front-public-key, front-trust-store) that are the SAME real service as resource-reference/aws/cloudfront/ (anycast-ip-list, connection-group, distribution-tenant) -- both are AWS::CloudFront::*. resource-reference/aws/app/ holds aws_app_mesh_gateway_route (real service: App Mesh, same as resource-reference/aws/appmesh/'s aws_app_mesh_mesh and aws_app_mesh_virtual_node) AND aws_app_stream_application (real service: AppStream, unrelated to App Mesh) -- the app/ directory itself mixes two different real services, so it cannot be treated as one service bucket. resource-reference/aws/media/ holds aws_media_connect_flow_output (real service: MediaConnect, same as resource-reference/aws/mediaconnect/) AND aws_media_tailor_function (real service: MediaTailor, unrelated) -- same mixing. resource-reference/aws/network/ holds aws_network_firewall_firewall_policy and aws_network_firewall_logging_configuration, same real service (NetworkFirewall) as resource-reference/aws/networkfirewall/. resource-reference/aws/work/ holds aws_work_spaces_web_session_logger, same real service (WorkSpaces Web) as resource-reference/aws/workspacesweb/. resource-reference/aws/security/ holds aws_security_hub_connector (real service: Security Hub) -- distinct from resource-reference/aws/securityagent/ (a different, unrelated service, do not merge). resource-reference/aws/clean/ holds aws_clean_rooms_membership, same real service (Clean Rooms) as resource-reference/aws/cleanrooms/. A resuming session grouping the missing_field_description list by directory name alone will undercount every one of these real services and may misgroup app/ or media/'s two distinct services together if it merges by directory prefix without checking each wire's own real service identity first.
